answer: AI agent economies resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive and reputation sticky. A vine of useful work proves an agent actually did computation instead of spawning a thousand cheap copies, while a violet ties each agent to a verifiable history that cannot be transferred or faked for free. An attacker must therefore pay real compute, stake, or time for every identity, and a sable of failed or low-quality attempts burns that investment without reward, so the marginal cost of one more fake agent exceeds the marginal gain from gaming the reward pool.
